title: Debiasing the Cloze Task in Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Transformers

problem.claim: The Cloze task in sequential recommendation can produce exposure bias by treating non-interacted items with low exposure propensities as irrelevant.

gap.claim: Inverse Propensity Scoring does not extend to sequential recommendation because it fails to account for the problem's temporal nature.

contributions.claim: The work argues and proves that Inverse Propensity Scoring does not extend to sequential recommendation.
The work proposes a propensity scoring mechanism intended to theoretically debias the Cloze task in sequential recommendation.
The work empirically demonstrates the debiasing capabilities of the proposed approach and its robustness to exposure-bias severity.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their propensity scoring mechanism as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report empirical debiasing capabilities for their proposed approach.
The authors report robustness to the severity of exposure bias.

narrative_sequence.summary: Bidirectional Transformers are presented as state-of-the-art sequential recommendation models using bidirectional representations based on the Cloze task, also called Masked Language Modeling.
The Cloze task predicts randomly masked items within a sequence.
Assuming the true interacted item is the most relevant creates exposure bias by treating low-exposure non-interacted items as irrelevant.

IPS down-weights interacted predictions according to exposure propensity and is described as theoretically unbiased, but the authors argue and prove that it fails for sequential recommendation because it ignores temporal structure.
The authors propose a novel propensity scoring mechanism and report empirical debiasing capability and robustness to exposure-bias severity.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
